messages:
sara-dev: Heads-up — customer asked for per-request visibility into why a request hit a fallback model variant (tier routing + region OOS -> modelB). They want this surfaced in the Console trace and in debug logs for customer-support. Is it safe to show the full fallback chain to customers?

mike-infra: We can surface a condensed chain (decision IDs + short reasons) in Console. I wouldn't return detailed internal heuristics in the customer-facing API response. Internal logs can keep the full trace.

kevin-plateng: Agree with mike. Proposal: add two fields to internal request metadata: `decision_id` (uuid) and `variant_chain` (array of variant names with reason tags). `decision_id` should be returned to customers as an opaque token for support, but `variant_chain` should be visible only in Console and support UI.

anjali-ux: For Console UX — show a compact breadcrumb above the request details: e.g. "tier:gold -> region:eu-west -> fallback:model-b-quant". Click expands to full timeline (timestamps + latency/skipped nodes). Avoid exposing heuristics like "prefers-quantized" text; use human-friendly reasons.

oliver-telemetry: Important: if we expose `decision_id` to customers, we need deterministic sampling to link customer-reported token to telemetry. Also we should tag spans with `routing.sample=1` when we keep full variant_chain in logs. Sampling rates: default 1% for hosted free-tier, 10% for paid tiers, and 100% for enterprise by contract. Thoughts?

mike-infra: sampling defaults SGTM. Implementation note: headers we emit today — `x-rd-trace` — are already noisy. I'd rather add a separate header `x-rd-route-id: <decision_id>` and keep variant details in `x-rd-route-meta` only for internal networks (VPC / private). That avoids leaking internal model names to shared-hosted responses.

kevin-plateng: Minor debate: should we make `decision_id` part of the stable API response envelope (`meta.routing_id`) or a header? Pros of envelope: easier for customers to parse in SDKs. Cons: API contract change and potential churn. Header keeps backward compatibility.

anjali-ux: If it's a header only, Console's request drilldown still needs to surface it. That's fine. For the UI copy: let's use "Routing snapshot (ID: <short>)" with a link to the detailed trace. Keep the default collapsed.

oliver-telemetry: Also flag: add `routing.reason` taxonomy to logs (strings only: tier_mismatch, regional_capacity, variant_quality, throttled). That makes alerting easier without exposing heuristics.

sara-dev: Implementation plan? Who owns the API/SDK change vs Console view vs telemetry?

mike-infra: Mike owns header + server-side instrumentation (I'll PR). Kevin takes API contract decision — if we go envelope we coordinate SDK bump.

kevin-plateng: I'll push a small RFC: option A header-only (no API bump), option B envelope + SDK minor. Recommend A to minimize churn.

anjali-ux: I'll mock the breadcrumb + expand panel. Need sample data shape — please include small example of `variant_chain` for mock.

mike-infra: Example header payload we can log internally: ```x-rd-route-meta: decision_id=dec-4b3f;chain="model-a:ok->model-b:capacity->model-b-quant:fallback";tier=gold;region=eu-west``` Use URL-safe csv? We should avoid JSON in headers.

oliver-telemetry: That's fine for logs. For structured telemetry events we'll emit JSON to our TSDB/observability backend: `{ "decision_id": "dec-4b3f", "chain": ["model-a","model-b","model-b-quant"], "reason": "regional_capacity", "sampled": true }` (internal only).

sara-dev: Two follow-ups: 1) Quota UI should show which tier routing impacted quota enforcement (e.g., gold->dedicated vs fallback->shared), 2) Rollout UX — console should be able to play back routing decisions across a canary window so PMs can see how many users hit fallback during canary.

mike-infra: For quota: we'll annotate per-request response in Console with `quota_source: dedicated_pool` vs `quota_source: shared_burst`. That can be fed to cost dashboards.

kevin-plateng: For rollout playback: we already have a trace export endpoint. Add filter param `?routing_id=dec-4b3f` and `?variant=model-b-quant` to find affected requests. We'll need to ensure retention matches enterprise SLAs.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-metadata-canary -> infra-canary-3 at 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z. Status: queued. :rocket:

anjali-ux: UX ask for telemetry: provide sample counts (n) next to each breadcrumb step so users can see how many requests traversed each hop in the canary window.

oliver-telemetry: Will add counts and p95 latency per hop. Note: counts must respect sampling — we will extrapolate using sampling factor. Document that in the export payload.

sara-dev: OK. Action items: mike PR for headers + instrumentation; kevin RFC for envelope decision (opt A preferred); anjali mocks by EOD Wednesday; oliver telemetry sampling config + export schema. I'll follow up with a short product note for support teams. Thanks! :thumbsup:
